title: Analytics & Visualization
subtitle: Episodes 4–6 in one place: analytics workloads, streaming and Power BI.

what.body: Analytics turns raw data into decisions in three moves: land the data, process it at the right speed, and show it so humans act. Episodes 4–6 cover each move: workloads and platforms, real-time streaming, and visualization.
what.example: Factory sensors stream readings (Episode 5), Spark crunches them at scale (Episode 4), and a live Power BI dashboard alerts the floor manager (Episode 6) — one pipeline, three episodes.

concepts.body: Any pipeline that ingests, processes, stores and analyzes data to produce insights — from nightly reports to live dashboards.
What happened → why → what will happen → what to do. Each step needs more modeling than the last.
Collect data over time, process it together on a schedule. Nightly sales summaries are the classic example.
Analyze an endless flow of events as they arrive, in seconds. Fraud detection and live telemetry live here.
A continuous sequence of events: sensor readings, clicks, card swipes. Unbounded — it never 'finishes'.
Chopping a stream into time slices (per minute, sliding 5 minutes) so aggregates like counts and averages work.
ETL transforms before loading; ELT lands raw data first and transforms inside the lake or warehouse at scale.

concepts.term: Data lake vs warehouse vs lakehouse
concepts.body: Lake = cheap raw storage of anything. Warehouse = curated structured data for reporting. Lakehouse = both at once.
A numeric calculation in Power BI: Total Sales, Average Order. The numbers you aggregate.
A categorical attribute you slice by: Region, Product, Month. The 'by' in every chart.
Leveled drill path such as Year → Quarter → Month for digging into detail.
Dataset = prepared data model. Report = multi-page interactive visuals. Dashboard = one page of pinned highlight tiles.

examples.title: Batch or stream?
examples.body: Morning sales summary = batch. Card-fraud block in 2 seconds = stream. Ask: does anyone act on each event instantly?

remember: Flow order: ingest → process → store → analyze → visualize.
Batch = scheduled chunks (Data Factory). Stream = always-on flow (Event Hubs → Stream Analytics → Power BI).
IoT Hub = Event Hubs + device management + two-way talk.
Report = multi-page deep dive · Dashboard = one page of pinned tiles.
Measure = number calculated · Dimension = category sliced by · Hierarchy = drill path.
Fabric = unified SaaS on OneLake · Databricks = Spark + notebooks · Parquet = analytic scans.

quickCheck.q: Fraud must be blocked per transaction in seconds: batch or stream?
quickCheck.a: Stream — Event Hubs plus Stream Analytics evaluates each event live.
Dataset feeds visuals; report explores across pages; dashboard pins highlights on one page.

quickCheck.q: 'Sales by Region, drilled to Month' — label each part?
quickCheck.a: Sales = measure, Region = dimension, Year→Month = hierarchy.

quickCheck.q: Keep raw clicks for unknown future questions: where?
quickCheck.a: A data lake — cheap raw retention.
